titulo: How your phone knows where you are with no internet 🛰️
descripcion: GPS is a one-way radio signal from satellites. Your phone just listens, measures timing from at least four satellites, and calculates its position.

escenas.texto: Turn off your data, and your phone still knows exactly where you are. How?
GPS doesn't use the internet at all. Satellites about twenty thousand kilometers up are constantly broadcasting the time.
Your phone just listens. It measures how long each signal took to arrive, and turns that into a distance.
With signals from at least four satellites, it can calculate your position on Earth.
The timing has to be insanely precise. Satellite clocks even need corrections for Einstein's relativity, or GPS would drift by kilometers every day.
So your map may need data, but your location doesn't. Follow for more tech secrets.
